title: Kalimpong Homestay Villages Compared
meta_description: Sillery Gaon, Icchey Gaon, Rishyap, Lava, Lolegaon and more compared: altitude, drive from Kalimpong, views, homestay rates and what to ask first.
summary: The villages around Kalimpong offer homestays at about ₹1,300–2,200 a person with dinner and breakfast. Ramdhura, Icchey Gaon and Sillery Gaon face the Teesta valley and Kanchenjunga within an hour or so of town; Lava, Kolakham and Rishyap are higher forest villages by Neora Valley; Lolegaon and Charkhole are quieter Lepcha villages further east.

sections.heading: Why base yourself in a village
paras: Kalimpong town is worth two nights: the haat on Wednesdays and Saturdays, the orchid and cactus nurseries, the monastery on Durpin hill, the old story of the Swiss dairy and its cheese. But the town sits at 1,247 m on a crowded ridge, and most of the views people come for are one to three hours away. Within 15–60 km of the motor stand, farming families in a dozen villages have turned spare rooms into homestays, and a night with dinner and breakfast costs about ₹1,300–2,200 a person. You eat what the house eats, usually rice, dal, a seasonal vegetable, squash or fern from the slope, and pickle, and you wake to a view a town hotel would charge double for.

The villages fall into three groups. East and south of town, toward Pedong, are Ramdhura, Icchey Gaon and Sillery Gaon: open ridges at 1,500–1,850 m facing the Teesta valley and Kanchenjunga. Further east, on the road to Neora Valley, are Lava, Kolakham and Rishyap, at 1,980–2,590 m, colder and greener, with forest on every side. Beyond Lava, Lolegaon and Charkhole are Lepcha villages among old oak and cypress, far enough out that most people stay two nights, not one. Pedong is a small market town rather than a homestay village, but it has history in every direction.

paras: Distances are rounded road kilometres from the Kalimpong motor stand; drive times assume a dry road and a reserved car. Homestay rates are indicative for 2025–26, per person with dinner and breakfast, and rise on long weekends and in October.

sections.heading: The Pedong side: Ramdhura, Icchey, Sillery
paras: Ramdhura and Icchey Gaon are neighbours about 2.5 km apart, and the easiest homestay villages to reach from town: 15–18 km, under an hour by car. Ramdhura, at about 1,525 m, takes its name from "Ram" and "dhura", a village, and looks over cinchona plantations and pine forest to the Teesta valley, with Kanchenjunga lit pink on clear mornings. Icchey Gaon, higher at about 1,770 m, is the birders' choice: flycatchers, sunbirds and woodpeckers work the trees around the houses, and a 6 km walk reaches the ruins of Damsang fort.

Sillery Gaon, at about 1,830 m and 5–6 km above Pedong, is the best known of the three and the busiest on long weekends. The local story says the name comes from the sillery plant that once grew here. Its pull is Ramitey Dara, a 3 km walk, from where the Teesta is seen making 14 bends (some people count 11). Shared jeeps run from Kalimpong to Pedong for ₹80–120 a seat; from Pedong you need a local car for the last climb. Pedong's Cross Hill, its old monastery and the fort are all within a short drive, so two nights here fill easily.

sections.heading: The Lava side: Lava, Kolakham and Rishyap
paras: Lava, at about 2,200 m and 30–34 km from Kalimpong via Algarah, is a small market and monastery town on the edge of Neora Valley National Park. It is cold from November to February and sees snow in some winters. The Kagyu Thekchen Ling monastery, opened in 1990, stands beside the Neora reservoir, and a weekly haat on Tuesday draws villages from around (check the day locally). Lava is where park permits and guides are arranged. Shared jeeps from the Kalimpong motor stand cost ₹120–180 a seat, but they are few and mostly leave in the morning; a reserved car is ₹2,500–3,000 one way.

Kolakham, 8 km beyond Lava at about 1,980 m, faces Kanchenjunga across the forest and is the quietest of the three. Local accounts say it was founded by Ujir Man Rai Samsuhang, and some still call it Rai Gaon. Changey Falls is about 4 km away. Rishyap, at 2,591 m, is the highest village in this guide; its Sherpa and Lepcha families began taking guests in 1998. Locals explain the name as "Ri", peak, and "shyap", old trees. You reach it by 10 km of road from Lava or a 4 km forest path uphill, and Tiffin Dara, 1 km from the houses, is the dawn viewpoint.

sections.heading: Lepcha country: Lolegaon and Charkhole
paras: Lolegaon, at about 1,675 m, is a Lepcha village 24 km from Lava and 55 km from Kalimpong; WBFDC made it known to travellers in the 1990s. Its heritage forest has a canopy walk, a hanging bridge of about 180 m strung through old oak and cypress, and Jhandi Dara, 4–5 km away, is the sunrise point. Charkhole, 12–15 km further at about 1,680 m, is smaller still, with a direct Kanchenjunga view and a forest walk to its viewpoint. A reserved car from Lava to Lolegaon costs ₹1,800–2,500.

We pair these two with Lava rather than with Kalimpong town: two nights in the Lava, Kolakham and Rishyap group, then one or two in Lolegaon or Charkhole, then down to Siliguri, about 124 km and 4 hours from Lolegaon. That saves the long drive back west and keeps each day's road time under three hours.

sections.heading: What to ask before you book
paras: Homestays here are family homes, not hotels, and a five-minute call saves most disappointments. Booking direct by phone is often a little cheaper than a listing site, and the whole payment stays with the family. In October and on long weekends the well-placed houses in Sillery Gaon, Rishyap and Kolakham fill weeks ahead, so book early; in July or January you can often ring the day before and still choose your room. These are the questions we ask on behalf of our travellers:
list: Is the rate per person or per room, and does it include dinner, breakfast and evening tea? Lunch is usually ₹150–250 extra.
Which rooms face the mountain, and is ours one of them? In Sillery Gaon and Rishyap the view rooms go first.
Is the bathroom attached, and is hot water from a geyser or a bucket? Above 2,000 m, winter nights drop close to freezing.
How far is the car drop from the door? Some houses are a 5–10 minute walk down steps, which matters with heavy bags or older parents.
Can the family arrange the next car or jeep, and at what rate?
Which mobile network works at the house? Signal changes from one ridge to the next.
What is the cancellation rule, and how much advance is needed by UPI?
Is there power backup? Cuts are common in monsoon storms.

sections.heading: Government lodges: WBTDC and WBFDC
paras: If you prefer a reception desk and a fixed tariff, the state runs six lodges in this part of the district. WBTDC, the West Bengal tourism corporation, has three in and around Kalimpong; WBFDC, the forest development corporation, runs eco tourism centres inside forest compounds. All are booked through the corporations' own websites. Rates below are indicative per room and change with season and room type; check current status before you travel.

Morgan House is the one people ask about: the ghost stories told about it are folklore, while the garden and the Durpin views are real. At the forest centres, meals are ordered ahead from the canteen and charged separately.

faqs.q: Which village near Kalimpong has the best Kanchenjunga view?
faqs.a: Rishyap, at 2,591 m, gives the widest view: from Tiffin Dara, 1 km from the village, the whole Kanchenjunga range is spread out at dawn. Charkhole has a direct, close view from the village itself, and Sillery Gaon adds the Teesta's bends from Ramitey Dara. All three need clear weather, which is most reliable from October to December and on spring mornings from March to May.

faqs.q: How much does a homestay in Sillery Gaon cost?
faqs.a: Expect about ₹1,500–2,200 a person a night with dinner and breakfast in 2025–26, a little more for a mountain-facing room on a long weekend. Lunch is usually ₹150–250 extra. Prices across the Kalimpong villages are similar, from about ₹1,300 a person in Ramdhura or Lolegaon. Always ask whether the quoted rate is per person or per room.

faqs.q: Should we stay in Lava or Rishyap?
faqs.a: Stay in Rishyap for the mountain view and quiet, and in Lava if you want the monastery, the Tuesday haat and easy access to Neora Valley permits. They are 10 km apart by road or 4 km by a forest path, so many travellers sleep in Rishyap and spend a day in Lava, or walk up from Lava with bags sent ahead by car.

faqs.q: Can we reach Sillery Gaon by shared jeep?
faqs.a: Partly. Shared jeeps run from the Kalimpong motor stand to Pedong for about ₹80–120 a seat and take about an hour. Sillery Gaon is 5–6 km above Pedong on a steep, narrow road, and for that last stretch you need a local car, which your homestay can usually arrange. A reserved car from Kalimpong straight to the village is the simpler option with luggage.

faqs.q: Are the Kalimpong villages suitable for older parents?
faqs.a: Most are, if you ask two questions first: how far the house is from the car drop, and whether the bathroom is attached with a geyser. Ramdhura and Icchey Gaon are lower, closer to town and gentler. Rishyap at 2,591 m is cold in winter and some homes there sit below the road down steps, so check before booking.

faqs.q: How do we book Morgan House or the Lava eco tourism centre?
faqs.a: Morgan House, Tashiding and Deolo Tourist Lodge are WBTDC properties, and the Lava, Lolegaon and Sailabash eco tourism centres belong to WBFDC; each corporation takes bookings through its own official website. Book early for October and long weekends. Room rates run from about ₹2,000 to ₹6,500 depending on the lodge and season; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: When is the best time to stay in the Kalimpong villages?
faqs.a: October to December gives the clearest mountain views and dry trails; March to May brings rhododendrons, birds and warmer nights. January and February are cold, with snow some years at Lava and Rishyap. From June to September rain, leeches and landslides make roads slow and views rare, though rates are lower and the forest is at its greenest.

faqs.q: How many nights should we spend in the villages?
faqs.a: We suggest at least two nights in each village group, because a single night means arriving tired in the afternoon mist and leaving before you have walked anywhere. A good shape for five nights is two in Kalimpong or Sillery Gaon, two in Rishyap or Kolakham, and one in Lolegaon before dropping to Siliguri.

faqs.q: Is the road to Kalimpong open after the Teesta floods?
faqs.a: NH10 via Teesta Bazar has had repeated landslide and flood closures since the October 2023 Teesta flood, including a slide near Coronation Bridge in June 2026. Drivers use diversions via Gorubathan and Lava, via Darjeeling and Peshok, or via Gajoldoba and Odlabari, which add one to three hours. Check current status before you travel.
